sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. sources.role: the owner's decisions, as narrowed by ruling:sam-2026-10-09: on look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour), overrides it. The prototype never decides architecture.

claims.statement: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype, the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1.
claims.quote: Goal: wherever the real services differ from Design Release 2.1, they change to match it.
claims.note: New: answers no earlier report question.

claims.statement: Which repos change (frontends, backends and other repos) is worked out from the evidence, not fixed in advance.
claims.quote: Work out from the evidence which frontends, backends and other repos that touches.
claims.note: New. The 'not fixed in advance' reading follows from 'work out from the evidence'.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements.
claims.quote: The DR1 parity backlog. [...] It is not a source of requirements.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Nothing is built because the DR1 parity backlog says so on its own; this follows from the backlog not being a source of requirements and being usable only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md lines 7-8 (DR1 paragraph); claim 3 second sentence
claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements. Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New. The main session's claim 3 states this in so many words; the quote implies it.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.quote: Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference between the real frontend and the prototype, the DR1 judgement is followed.
claims.quote: if DR1 already made a judgement on that difference, follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where a DR1 judgement is followed, the DR1 parity backlog row it comes from is cited.
claims.quote: follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.
claims.note: New. 'Over what the real services do today' is the main session's framing; it follows from the Goal paragraph.

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. 'On the same difference' comes from the DR1 paragraph (lines 8-9).

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: The frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled, refusing only an entirely empty animal with "Enter at least one identifier for this animal", which matches the V4 field block "Field Block - Mandatory to Submit - At least one Animal Identifier".
claims.quote: One identifier is enough. A trader who fills the ear tag and leaves the passport blank presses "Save and add another", the animal is added to the summary list as "Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012", and the counter moves on to "Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2". Only an entirely empty animal is refused, with "Enter at least one identifier for this animal"

claims.statement: Design release 1 counts an animal as entered only when every identifier for its commodity has a value, shows no error for a partly filled animal, keeps the trader on that animal with the counter unmoved, and lists only complete animals in the saved table.
claims.quote: An animal counts as entered only when every identifier declared for its commodity carries a value (app/routes.js:1526-1532), so a cattle animal needs both an ear tag and a passport and a horse needs a microchip, a passport and a horse name. A partly filled animal is not refused and no error is shown — the page simply re-renders the same animal with the values kept and the counter unmoved, and the saved-animals table lists only complete animals.

claims.statement: If every identifier is ruled required, the work is: each individual identifier becomes mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary, new error copy is written (Design release 1 supplies none), and the change follows the correction of the commodity identifier sets (inc-110), since otherwise it would demand a tattoo for every cow.
claims.ref: backlog.json inc-103, finding.difference and finding.relatedTo inc-110
claims.quote: move the individual identifier obligations from optional to mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary rather than the record failing as a whole, and write the error copy for it, which Design release 1 does not supply because it shows no message at all; if they are not required, Frontend is already right and this finding should be struck. Any such change also has to follow the commodity identifier sets being corrected, because the rule is only as good as the set it ranges over — with tattoo still on cattle it would demand a tattoo for every cow.

claims.note: Corrects repo-tests-p1-154. The permanent address page itself belongs to part 2.

sources.role: how the real animals frontend renders today

claims.statement: The identification page is reached from the Overview task list by a task row link named 'Identification details', which sits second under '2. Description of the goods', after 'Commodity details'.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377; overview snapshot, task id description-of-the-goods-2-status
claims.quote: Identification details

claims.statement: The Identification details task row shows the status 'To do' (blue tag) before any animal is identified.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) overview before call@1377, description-of-the-goods-2-status
claims.quote: To do

claims.statement: Once every animal on the only identifiable line has a saved record, the Identification details task row shows 'Complete' (green tag).
claims.ref: trace a783b (identification.fit.spec.js:503) overview after call@1649, description-of-the-goods-2-status
claims.quote: Complete

claims.statement: The identification page lives at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/commodities/identification.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) network, GET after the Identification details click
claims.quote: GET http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-D09581/commodities/identification 200

claims.statement: The page's browser title is 'Identification details - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.ref: trace e3b1e (identification.fit.spec.js:394) TITLE element on the identification page
claims.quote: Identification details - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: When the page shows an error summary its browser title is prefixed with 'Error: '.
claims.ref: trace fdf5c (identification.fit.spec.js:835) TITLE after the stale add action
claims.quote: Error: Identification details - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The page heading (h1, govuk-heading-l) is 'Identification details'.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot, main h1
claims.quote: Identification details

claims.statement: The heading carries the section caption 'About the consignment'.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot, span.govuk-caption-l
claims.quote: About the consignment

claims.statement: The caption 'About the consignment' does not match the Overview section the task row sits in ('2. Description of the goods').
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 before and after snapshots
claims.quote: About the consignment
claims.note: Read from the two rendered pages side by side; the trace does not say which wording is intended.

claims.statement: Above the caption the page shows the journey strip: a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification reference in bold.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot, div.app-journey-strip
claims.quote: Draft GBN-AG-26-D09581

claims.statement: Below the heading an inset text tells the trader all identification details must be added before arrival at the port of entry.
claims.quote: You must add all animal identification details before the consignment arrives at the port of entry.

claims.statement: The page has a back link 'Back' that returns to the notification's Overview.
claims.quote: "href":"/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-PVF54S","class":"govuk-back-link"},"Back"

claims.statement: The page opens with a 'Selected commodities' table (caption size m) listing every commodity line in the consignment, placed before the first identification card.
claims.quote: Selected commodities

claims.statement: The Selected commodities table has the column headings 'Commodity code', 'Common name' and 'Number of animals', plus a visually hidden 'Actions' column.
claims.ref: trace 7044e (identification.fit.spec.js:553) call@1403, call@1405, call@1407; dd986 call@1377 snapshot
claims.quote: Commodity code | Common name | Number of animals | Actions

claims.statement: Each Selected commodities row shows the commodity code, the common name and the number of animals entered on Commodity details, for example cattle as '0102', 'Domestic cattle', '2' and horse as '0101', 'Horse', '3'.
claims.quote: 0102 Domestic cattle 2 ... 0101 Horse 3

claims.statement: The Selected commodities table also lists a commodity that has nothing to identify, such as Atlantic salmon (0301), even though that line gets no identification card.
claims.quote: 0301 Atlantic salmon 1

claims.statement: Each Selected commodities row has a 'Change' link (visually hidden suffix naming the common name, e.g. 'Change Domestic cattle') that goes to the What are you importing? page at /commodities.
claims.quote: Change Domestic cattle

claims.statement: Below the summary table an 'Add another commodity' link goes to the What are you importing? page, and it shows while there are commodities to identify.
claims.quote: Add another commodity

claims.statement: Each commodity line that has identifiers gets its own card section (id identification-card-<line index>) headed '<Common name> (<code>) — <species>', for example 'Cow (0102) — Bos taurus'.
claims.quote: Cow (0102) — Bos taurus

claims.statement: The card heading uses a different common name from the summary table for the same cattle line: 'Cow' on the card, 'Domestic cattle' in Selected commodities.
claims.quote: Domestic cattle ... Cow (0102) — Bos taurus
claims.note: Recorded as rendered; whether the two names should agree is for the reconciler.

claims.statement: A commodity line with no identifier of its own (Atlantic salmon, Salmo salar) gets no identification card and no address fields.
claims.quote: #identification-card-2 to.have.count

claims.statement: When no line in the consignment has anything to identify, the Overview leaves out the Identification details task row.
claims.ref: trace dcde6 (identification.fit.spec.js:447) overview snapshot before call@1391
claims.quote: 2. Description of the goods ... Commodity details ... Additional details

claims.statement: Requesting the identification page directly for a consignment with nothing to identify redirects (302) to the Overview instead of showing the page.
claims.ref: trace dcde6 (identification.fit.spec.js:447) call@1391 to call@1395; network
claims.quote: GET .../GBN-AG-26-VSMR3P/commodities/identification 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-VSMR3P

claims.statement: Every card has a 'Change number of animals' link (visually hidden suffix naming the card heading) that goes to the Commodity details page at /consignment-details.
claims.quote: Change number of animals

claims.statement: Following Change number of animals lands on the Commodity details page with the line's saved count prefilled.
claims.quote: #numberOfAnimalsQuantity-0 to.have.value 2

claims.statement: Each card asks for one animal at a time under an h3 counter 'Enter details for <species> N of M', where M is the line's number of animals and N the next animal without a record.
claims.quote: Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 2

claims.statement: A cattle line (Bos taurus) asks for exactly two identifiers, ear tag first then passport, and no tattoo or microchip.
claims.ref: trace b2d23 (identification.fit.spec.js:278) call@661; trace dd986 call@1383 to call@1393
claims.quote: Ear tag || Passport

claims.statement: A horse line (Equus caballus) asks for microchip number, passport and horse name, in that order.
claims.quote: Microchip number || Passport || Horse name

claims.statement: A cat line (Felis catus) asks for microchip number, passport and tattoo, in that order.
claims.quote: Microchip number ... Passport ... Tattoo

claims.statement: A dog line (Canis lupus familiaris) asks for the same identifiers as a cat: microchip number, passport and tattoo.
claims.quote: Microchip number ... Passport ... Tattoo

claims.statement: The ear tag field is labelled 'Ear tag' (bold small label) with the hint 'For example, UK123456789012'; it is a 20-character-wide text input named animalIdentifierEarTag-<line>.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot; trace 19c03 call@1305
claims.quote: Ear tag For example, UK123456789012

claims.statement: The passport field is labelled 'Passport' with the hint 'For example, UK123456789'; it is a 20-character-wide text input named animalIdentifierPassport-<line>.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot; trace 19c03 call@1303
claims.quote: Passport For example, UK123456789

claims.statement: The microchip field is labelled 'Microchip number' with the hint 'For example, 900123456789012'; it is a 20-character-wide text input named animalIdentifierMicrochip-<line>.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot (horse card)
claims.quote: Microchip number For example, 900123456789012

claims.statement: The tattoo field is labelled 'Tattoo' with the hint 'For example, AB1234'; it is a 20-character-wide text input named animalIdentifierTattoo-<line>.
claims.quote: Tattoo For example, AB1234

claims.statement: The horse name field is labelled 'Horse name', has no hint, and is a 20-character-wide text input named horseName-<line>.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 after snapshot (horse card)
claims.quote: Horse name

claims.statement: Identifier inputs are keyed by the commodity line index, not the animal: the same input (e.g. animalIdentifierEarTag-0) is reused for each successive animal on the line.
claims.quote: fill #animalIdentifierEarTag-0 UK000000000001 ... fill #animalIdentifierEarTag-0 UK000000000002

claims.statement: The microchip entry label 'Microchip number' differs from its saved-animals column heading 'Microchip', while passport and ear tag use the same words in both places.
claims.ref: trace 07a52 (identification.fit.spec.js:723) call@1747 snapshot; trace 19c03 call@1303 to call@1305
claims.quote: Microchip number ... Microchip
claims.note: The spec comment says Design release 1 has not settled the microchip entry wording.

claims.statement: Cattle and horse cards ask for no permanent address; only cat and dog cards show the permanent address block.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1399; trace b2704 call@1453 snapshot; trace bfdf8 call@1339 snapshot
claims.quote: #nameOrOrganisationName-0 to.have.count

claims.statement: The permanent address block opens with a warning text (govuk-warning-text) saying a false address is fraud.
claims.quote: Providing a false address is an act of fraud

claims.statement: The warning is followed by guidance defining a permanent address as where the animal will permanently reside and can be checked by APHA, as a bulleted list.
claims.quote: A permanent address is where an animal: will permanently reside | can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)

claims.statement: The address fields sit under the h3 question 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
claims.quote: Where will their permanent address be?

claims.statement: The permanent address asks for eight fields in this order: Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Phone number, Email address.
claims.ref: trace bfdf8 (identification.fit.spec.js:320) call@1343 to call@1357 and call@1339 snapshot
claims.quote: Name or organisation name | Address line 1 | Address line 2 (optional) | Town or city | County (optional) | Postcode or Zip code | Phone number | Email address

claims.statement: Address line 2 and County are marked optional in their labels; the other six address fields carry no optional marker.
claims.quote: Address line 2 (optional) ... County (optional)

claims.statement: The permanent address never asks for a country, and the page has no select control at all.
claims.quote: #country-0 to.have.count ... select to.have.count

claims.statement: The phone number field has the hint 'For international numbers include the country code' as its accessible description.
claims.quote: For international numbers include the country code

claims.statement: The postcode field is labelled 'Postcode or Zip code' and is a 10-character-wide input with autocomplete postal-code.
claims.ref: trace b2ce6 (identification.fit.spec.js:335) call@1391; trace bfdf8 call@1339 snapshot
claims.quote: Postcode or Zip code

claims.statement: Address inputs carry browser autocomplete tokens: name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 (town or city), postal-code, tel and email; County has none. Phone is type tel and email is type email.
claims.quote: autocomplete="name" ... autocomplete="address-line1" ... autocomplete="address-line2" ... autocomplete="address-level2" ... autocomplete="postal-code" ... type="tel" ... autocomplete="tel" ... type="email" ... autocomplete="email"

claims.statement: Address inputs are sized by field: name, address lines and email full width; town or city and county two-thirds width; postcode 10 characters; phone 20 characters.
claims.quote: govuk-input ... govuk-!-width-two-thirds ... govuk-input--width-10 ... govuk-input--width-20

claims.statement: Each animal on a cat or dog line has its own permanent address: after one animal is saved, the next animal's address fields are empty again.
claims.quote: Enter details for Felis catus 2 of 2 ... nameOrOrganisationName-0 ... value=""

claims.statement: While a line has more than one animal still without a record, the card ends with a secondary in-card button 'Save and add another'.
claims.quote: Save and add another

claims.statement: On the last animal a line still owes, the in-card button reads 'Save and finish' instead, and 'Save and add another' is gone.
claims.quote: Save and finish

claims.statement: A line of exactly one animal shows no in-card button at all ('1 of 1'); the page's Save and continue saves that animal's record.
claims.quote: Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 1

claims.statement: Both in-card buttons submit the same action, add:<line index>, so 'Save and add another' and 'Save and finish' differ only in wording.
claims.quote: value="add:0" name="action" ... Save and finish

claims.statement: Saving a record with an in-card button posts the whole form to the identification URL and redirects (302) back to the same page, which re-renders with the record in the table and the counter moved on.
claims.quote: POST .../commodities/identification 302 .../commodities/identification

claims.statement: When every animal on a line has a record, the card drops the entry fields and the in-card button and shows a completion line naming the count and species.
claims.ref: trace 05b15 (identification.fit.spec.js:473) call@1497; trace 0e965 call@2087 to call@2089
claims.quote: You have entered details for all 2 Bos taurus animals. Remove a record if you need to replace it.

claims.statement: For a line of one animal the completion line reads 'all 1 Bos taurus animals', with no singular form.
claims.quote: You have entered details for all 1 Bos taurus animals. Remove a record if you need to replace it.

claims.statement: Once a line has at least one record, the card shows a saved-animals table above the entry fields, with one row per saved animal.
claims.quote: Animal | Ear tag | Passport ... Bos taurus 1 | UK000000000001

claims.statement: Before any record is saved the card shows no saved-animals table.
claims.ref: trace bfdf8 (identification.fit.spec.js:320) call@1339 snapshot; trace 285e7 (identification.fit.spec.js:818) call@1897 snapshot
claims.quote: Enter details for Felis catus 1 of 2
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of a table in the rendered card when no record exists, including straight after the only record is removed.

claims.statement: The saved-animals table's first column is 'Animal' and each row is named '<species> <number>', for example 'Bos taurus 1'.
claims.quote: Animal ... Bos taurus 1

claims.statement: The saved-animals table has a column for every identifier the commodity declares, in the commodity's own order, even when a record left that identifier blank: cattle 'Ear tag', 'Passport'; cat and dog 'Microchip', 'Passport', 'Tattoo'.
claims.ref: trace 26bc8 (identification.fit.spec.js:764) call@1815 to call@1821; trace 07a52 call@1747 to call@1753
claims.quote: Animal | Ear tag | Passport ... Animal | Microchip | Passport | Tattoo | Permanent address

claims.statement: For cat and dog the saved-animals table adds a 'Permanent address' column, which shows only the name or organisation name (e.g. 'Pet Owner'), not the full address.
claims.ref: trace 07a52 (identification.fit.spec.js:723) call@1755, call@1761 and call@1747 snapshot
claims.quote: Permanent address ... Pet Owner

claims.statement: A blank identifier on a saved record shows as an empty cell in the saved-animals table.
claims.quote: Bos taurus 1 | UK000000000001 |

claims.statement: A cat record with microchip, passport and a full permanent address saves and reads back its microchip number, passport number and owner name in its row.
claims.quote: Felis catus 1 | 900123456789012 | UK123456789 | | Pet Owner

claims.statement: A dog identified only by its microchip number, with a permanent address and no passport or tattoo, is accepted and saved.
claims.quote: Canis lupus familiaris 1 | 900123456789012 | | | Pet Owner

claims.statement: A cattle animal identified only by its ear tag, with no passport, is accepted and saved.
claims.quote: animalIdentifierEarTag-0=UK000000000001 ... animalIdentifierPassport-0=

claims.statement: Saved records persist on the server: after a page reload the saved dog's microchip still shows in its row.
claims.quote: reload ... Canis lupus familiaris 1 ... 900123456789012

claims.statement: Each saved-animals row has a 'Remove' control (a button styled as a link, visually hidden suffix ' animal <n>') that submits action remove:<line>:<record index>.
claims.quote: Remove animal 1 ... action=remove:0:0

claims.statement: Remove deletes the record straight away with no confirmation step; the page reloads without the row and the counter steps back.
claims.ref: trace 285e7 (identification.fit.spec.js:818) call@1895 to call@1897 and snapshot
claims.quote: POST .../commodities/identification 302 ... Enter details for Felis catus 1 of 2

claims.statement: Saved records cannot be edited in place: the saved-animals row offers only Remove, and the completion line tells the trader to remove a record to replace it.
claims.quote: Remove a record if you need to replace it.

claims.statement: Removing a record from a full line reopens entry for that line: the counter returns to the removed slot ('2 of 2') and the in-card 'Save and finish' button comes back.
claims.ref: trace 0e965 (identification.fit.spec.js:853) call@2105 to call@2107 and snapshot
claims.quote: Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2 ... Save and finish

claims.statement: An add action posted for a line that already has a record for every animal is rejected: the page re-renders (200, no redirect) with an error summary 'There is a problem' and saves nothing.
claims.ref: trace fdf5c (identification.fit.spec.js:835) call@1943 to call@1945; network POST 200
claims.quote: You have already entered details for all 2 animals — remove a record before adding another

claims.statement: The cap-reached error summary link points to the line's card (#identification-card-<line>), and no inline error message is shown on the card.
claims.ref: trace fdf5c (identification.fit.spec.js:835) call@1947 to call@1949 and call@1945 snapshot
claims.quote: <a href="#identification-card-0">You have already entered details for all 2 animals — remove a record before adding another

claims.statement: On Commodity details, lowering a line's number of animals below the number of saved identification records is blocked with an error on the count field.
claims.ref: trace 0e965 (identification.fit.spec.js:853) call@2097 to call@2101 and snapshot
claims.quote: You have 2 identifier records for Bos taurus but entered 1 animal. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.

claims.statement: The count-drop error summary link goes to the identification page, anchored at the line's card (/commodities/identification#identification-card-<line>).
claims.quote: href="/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-62GPV9/commodities/identification#identification-card-0"

claims.statement: A rejected count drop keeps the earlier saved count: the identification page still shows 2 animals for the line after the trader followed the error.
claims.quote: 0102 Domestic cattle 2

claims.statement: The page ends with a button group: primary 'Save and continue', secondary 'Save and return to overview', and the link 'Cancel and return to overview' to the Overview.
claims.ref: trace 66033 (identification.fit.spec.js:380) call@1055; trace dd986 call@1377 snapshot
claims.quote: Save and continue | Save and return to overview | Cancel and return to overview

claims.statement: Save and continue posts the form and redirects (302) to the Overview.
claims.ref: trace a783b (identification.fit.spec.js:503) network POST; trace 0e965 network
claims.quote: POST .../commodities/identification 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-PWZVT2

claims.statement: Save and continue with filled entry fields on a line saves them as that line's next record (no action field is sent).
claims.ref: trace a783b (identification.fit.spec.js:503) network POST, call@1651 snapshot
claims.quote: concurrencyToken=0&animalIdentifierEarTag-0=UK000000000001&animalIdentifierPassport-0=

claims.statement: The form starts with a visually hidden submit button 'Save and finish' (action finish), so pressing Enter in a field triggers that action rather than an in-card add.
claims.quote: <button type="submit" name="action" value="finish" class="govuk-visually-hidden">Save and finish
claims.note: Inferred from HTML implicit-submission rules (the first submit button is the default); no trace presses Enter, so what 'finish' does is unseen.

claims.statement: The form posts as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with a CSRF crumb and a hidden concurrencyToken, which stayed 0 across every save in these traces.
claims.quote: crumb=[REDACTED] ... {"name":"concurrencyToken","value":"0"}
claims.note: Crumb value redacted. A token that never moves after saves may mean it is not a per-save version; the trace cannot say.

claims.statement: The form is novalidate, so browser-side validation is off and every check happens on the server.
claims.quote: <form method="post" novalidate="">

claims.statement: The page has no serious or critical axe accessibility violations with a cattle line, with a cat's microchip field rendered, on the last outstanding animal, and once an animal is saved.
claims.quote: has no serious or critical axe violations
claims.note: The traces show axe running; the source records every test as passed, which is where the result comes from.

claims.statement: Apart from govuk-frontend components (table, inset text, warning text, inputs, hints, buttons, button group, back link, tag, section break) the page uses three non-standard pieces: the 'app-journey-strip' header strip, 'app-link-button' (a submit button styled as a link for Remove), and a visually hidden default submit button.
claims.ref: trace dd986 (identification.fit.spec.js:245) call@1377 snapshot; trace 05b15 call@1487 snapshot
claims.quote: app-journey-strip ... govuk-link app-link-button ... class="govuk-visually-hidden">Save and finish

claims.statement: Cards are separated by a visible large section break, and each card is a plain section, not a govuk summary card.
claims.quote: <section id="identification-card-0" class="govuk-!-margin-bottom-6"> ... govuk-section-break govuk-section-break--l govuk-section-break--visible

claims.statement: The browser only talks to the frontend; the backend calls that persist identification records cannot be seen in these traces.
No trace presses 'Save and return to overview' or 'Cancel and return to overview', so whether either saves the entry fields is unseen.
No trace walks a ferret line or any species other than cattle, horse, cat, dog and salmon, so their identifier sets are unseen.
claims.note: The spec comment names cat, dog and ferret as sharing the tattoo code.

claims.statement: No trace fills a tattoo or horse name and reads it back, so how those values show in the saved-animals table is unseen; no horse record is saved at all, so the horse table's columns are unseen.
No trace shows the Identification details task status for a partly identified consignment (some animals saved, some not), so any 'In progress' state is unseen.
No trace saves records on two cards at once or uses the second card's in-card button (add:1), so multi-line saving is unseen.
claims.ref: trace b2704 (identification.fit.spec.js:403) call@1453 snapshot shows add:1 but it is never pressed

claims.statement: Submitting the identification page with a validation error re-renders the same page (HTTP 200 on the POST, no redirect) at the identification URL.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-6ecc5 network POST /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-RR2J3A/commodities/identification; same in all 21 traces
claims.quote: POST http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-RR2J3A/commodities/identification -> 200

claims.statement: On a validation failure the page title is prefixed with 'Error: '.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-6ecc5 frame snapshot call@1587 TITLE
claims.quote: Error: Identification details - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: On a validation failure a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem' appears at the top of main, above the caption and heading.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-6ecc5 frame snapshot call@1587 main
claims.quote: There is a problem

claims.statement: Each error summary entry is a link whose href is the id of the field in error on that card (for example #animalIdentifierMicrochip-0), and clicking it moves focus to that field.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-6ecc5 actions pw:api@63 (click summary link) and expect@64 (toBeFocused #animalIdentifierMicrochip-0)
claims.quote: <A href=#animalIdentifierMicrochip-0>Enter at least one identifier for this animal

claims.statement: Each field in error gets an inline error message above its input, with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the error modifier on its form group and input, and the error message id added to the input's aria-describedby after any hint.
claims.quote: animalIdentifierMicrochip-0-error ' Error: Enter at least one identifier for this animal ' ... govuk-input govuk-input--width-20 govuk-input--error ... describedby=animalIdentifierMicrochip-0-hint animalIdentifierMicrochip-0-error

claims.statement: Pressing 'Save and add another' on a cat card with every identifier and every address field empty fails with one error asking for at least one identifier.
claims.quote: Enter at least one identifier for this animal

claims.statement: The at-least-one-identifier error links to and focuses the first identifier field on the card; for a cat that is the microchip number field.
claims.quote: #animalIdentifierMicrochip-0 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal'

claims.statement: With the record wholly empty, the at-least-one-identifier error is the only error shown: no address-field errors appear although every mandatory address field was blank, so the empty-address checks are not reported alongside the missing-identifier error.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-6ecc5 call@1587 SUMMARY and ERRGROUPS (1 error group)
claims.quote: SUMMARY: #animalIdentifierMicrochip-0 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal'
claims.note: Inferred from one error summary entry and one error form group while nameOrOrganisationName-0, addressLine1-0, townOrCity-0, postalOrZipCode-0, telephoneNumber-0 and emailAddress-0 were all posted empty.

claims.statement: After the at-least-one-identifier error the microchip field is still empty.
claims.quote: animalIdentifierMicrochip-0=(0)[govuk-input govuk-input--width-20 govuk-input--error]

claims.statement: A microchip number over 58 characters fails validation.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-4ee49 (identification.fit.spec.js:636, Microchip) call@863 error summary
claims.quote: Microchip must be 58 characters or fewer

claims.statement: A tattoo over 58 characters fails validation.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-9f957 (identification.fit.spec.js:636, Tattoo) call@1599 error summary
claims.quote: Tattoo must be 58 characters or fewer

claims.statement: A passport number over 58 characters fails validation.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-515ca (identification.fit.spec.js:636, Passport) call@1745 error summary
claims.quote: Passport must be 58 characters or fewer

claims.statement: An ear tag over 58 characters fails validation.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-422d3 (identification.fit.spec.js:636, Ear tag) call@1263 error summary
claims.quote: Ear tag must be 58 characters or fewer

claims.statement: A horse name over 58 characters fails validation.
claims.ref: trace commodities-fit-identifica-823bf (identification.fit.spec.js:636, Horse name) call@1513 error summary
claims.quote: Horse name must be 58 characters or fewer

claims.statement: Each over-length identifier error links to and focuses its own identifier field, and the field keeps the 59-character value the user entered.
claims.ref: traces 4ee49, 9f957, 515ca, 422d3, 823bf: INPUTS show the 59-character value with govuk-input--error; spec line 644-649 expectErrorFocus then toHaveValue(invalid)

claims.statement: The trace never shows validation of an identifier's format: no invalid ear tag, passport, microchip or tattoo was submitted, so any format rule and its error copy is unseen.
The trace never shows a dog line: the cats-and-dogs permanent address rule was walked for cats only, so the dog unit form's identifier types and permanent address are unseen.
The trace never shows a horse line or any other species with its own identifier set, so the commodities that get a 'Horse name' field (asserted absent for cats) and their form are unseen.
The trace never shows a consignment with two or more identifier-bearing lines, so how multiple cards stack on the page is unseen.

claims.statement: The trace never shows which commodities other than cattle trigger CPH, or any CPH validation beyond an empty submission (partial entry, non-numeric, wrong length).
The trace never exercises 'Save and return to overview' or 'Cancel and return to overview' on the identification page, nor what happens to an unsaved record when the user leaves.
The trace never shows what happens to identifier records or the CPH number when the triggering commodity line is removed.
